title: 新添声杨柳枝词·其二（井底点灯深烛伊）
titlePy: Xīn Tiān Shēng Yáng Liǔ Zhī Cí · Qí Èr
titleEn: Willow Branch, Newly Set to Music (No. 2)
author: 温庭筠
intro: A woman begs her man not to stay away too long — but almost every line says it through a pun. It ends with one of the best-known love lines in Chinese: red beans set in dice of bone, “longing that goes to the bone — do you know?”
analysis: 这首诗是一个女子对即将远行的爱人说的话，妙在几乎每一句都用了“双关”——一个词同时有两个意思。第一句“井底点灯深烛伊”：在井底点灯，是“深烛”，听起来像“深嘱”，意思是“我深深地嘱咐你”（伊：你）。第二句“共郎长行莫围棋”：“长行”是一种古代的博戏，也是“长久远行”；“围棋”谐音“违期”，就是不按时回来。表面说“陪你玩长行，别下围棋”，实际是说“你出远门，千万别误了归期”。第三、四句最有名：精巧的骰子是骨头做的，上面嵌着红色的点，像一颗颗红豆。红豆在中国又叫“相思豆”，象征思念；骰子是骨头做的，所以说“入骨相思”——思念已经深入骨头。最后一问“知不知”，又娇嗔又真诚。整首诗用游戏的语言说最认真的感情，十分俏皮动人。
analysisEn: A woman speaks to the man she loves before he leaves on a journey, and nearly every line hides a pun — one phrase carrying two meanings. Line one: “lighting a lamp deep in a well” is 深烛 shēn zhú, which sounds like 深嘱 shēn zhǔ, “I earnestly urge you”; 伊 means “you”. Line two plays with two board games. 长行 was a popular dice game, but the words also mean “a long journey”; 围棋 (weiqi, the game of Go) sounds like 违期 wéi qī, “to miss the agreed date”. So “play changxing with me, not weiqi” secretly means “on your long trip, don’t miss the day you promised to come back.” The last two lines are the famous ones. Fine dice were made of bone, with red pips inlaid like little red beans. In Chinese, red beans are called “love-longing beans”, and since the dice are bone, the longing has gone “into the bone”. She ends with a question — “do you know, or not?” — half teasing, half pleading. Serious love, said in the playful language of games: that is the charm of this little song.
background: Wen Tingyun (c. 812–866) wrote many lyrics to popular tunes of his day. The “Willow Branch” was a well-known tune; “newly added sounds” means it was a newer, expanded musical version. This is the second of two pieces in the set, both written in a woman’s voice.
pronunciation: 骰子 tóu zi（不读 shǎi，口语“色子 shǎi zi”是另一种说法）；伊 yī（你）；烛 zhú。“长行”是古代一种博戏名，网站读 cháng xíng，与“远行”双关（有注本将博戏“长行”读作 cháng háng）。机器朗读“长行”可能读成 cháng háng，已在“朗读用字”列替换为“常行”，音频需人工听验。
version: 采用通行版本，题作《新添声杨柳枝词二首》其二。其一为“一尺深红胜曲尘”。

lines.py: jǐng dǐ diǎn dēng shēn zhú yī
lines.lit: At the bottom of a well I light a lamp — deep candle (= I earnestly urge) you:
lines.en: A lamp lit deep in a well — so deep is what I ask of you:

lines.py: gòng láng cháng xíng mò wéi qí
lines.lit: with you I play changxing (= on your long journey), not weiqi (= don’t miss the date).
lines.en: go off on your long journey, love, but don’t you miss the day you’re due.

lines.py: líng lóng tóu zi ān hóng dòu
lines.lit: Exquisite dice are set with red beans;
lines.en: Into these delicate dice of bone, red beans are set —

lines.py: rù gǔ xiāng sī zhī bù zhī
lines.lit: longing that enters the bone — do you know or not?
lines.en: a longing gone into the bone. Do you know? Do you?

words.en: a light deep down — a pun on 深嘱 “to urge earnestly”

words.note: 古代第三人称或第二人称代词；今天书面语偶尔还用“伊人”。
现代汉语说“和……一起”，“共同”里还有这个意思。

words.en: my man; darling (a woman’s word for her husband or lover)
a dice board game; also “a long journey” (pun)
words.note: 双关：一种博戏，又指出远门。

words.en: weiqi (Go) — a pun on 违期 “to miss the date”
words.note: 今天的“围棋”；这里谐音“违期”（误了约定的日期）。
现代汉语仍用，如“小巧玲珑”。
现代汉语仍用，口语也说“色子 shǎizi”。
又叫“相思豆”；这里指骰子上的红点。

words.en: longing that goes into the bone
words.note: 今天仍常引用，形容思念极深。

imagery.name: 灯
imagery.zh: 井底的一盏灯，借“深烛”谐音“深嘱”，把叮嘱说得又深又切。
imagery.en: A lamp at the bottom of a well: through the pun 深烛 / 深嘱, it becomes her deep, heartfelt request.

imagery.name: 红豆
imagery.zh: 骰子上的红点像红豆，红豆就是相思；又因骰子是骨制的，相思“入骨”。
imagery.en: The red pips on the dice are like red beans — the bean of longing — and since the dice are bone, the longing goes to the bone.
